analysis_notes: Based on alternative_evaluation.json; statuses and impacts are cited from it rather than re-evaluated.

All reasoning is qualitative. No performance, availability, cost or energy measurements exist in the inputs; no quantitative superiority is claimed. Counts below are tallies of evaluation statuses, not measurements.

A1.requirements: 10 satisfied (S2, S4, S6-S13), 3 partially_satisfied (S1, S3, S5), 0 not_satisfied
A1.high_priority_drivers: 3 satisfied (consistency, payment integration, multi-channel), 2 partially_satisfied (data protection/compliance, bike location tracking/unlocking)

A2.requirements: 9 satisfied (S2, S4, S7-S13), 4 partially_satisfied (S1, S3, S5, S6), 0 not_satisfied
A2.high_priority_drivers: 3 satisfied (data protection/compliance, payment integration, multi-channel), 2 partially_satisfied (consistency, bike location tracking/unlocking)

A3.requirements: 10 satisfied (S2, S4, S5, S7-S13), 3 partially_satisfied (S1, S3, S6), 0 not_satisfied
A3.high_priority_drivers: 3 satisfied (consistency, payment integration, bike location tracking/unlocking - conditional on connected bikes), 2 partially_satisfied (data protection/compliance, multi-channel)

evaluation_summary.shared_partial_requirements: S1 (end-to-end encryption reading unconfirmed) and S3 (on-device biometric matching assumed) are partially_satisfied in every alternative; they do not discriminate between alternatives and depend on requirement clarification.

strengths: Strongest data consistency: single authoritative store, atomic registration and same-transaction read models make S7 immediate and keep biker (S5) and administrator (S12) views consistent without relying on any eventual-consistency assumption (evaluation: consistency driver satisfied; consistency QA positive).
Ties A3 for the most satisfied requirements (10 of 13) and is the only alternative that explicitly allocates navigation guidance (maps/navigation adapter), so S6 is satisfied.
Explicitly resolves the S4 vs S9 conflict by delivering notifications over session-independent channels.
Lowest structural complexity and runtime footprint: in-process calls (timeliness QA positive) and the only alternative satisfying the carbon-footprint driver under the resource-efficiency reading.
Integration variability (payment platforms, SMS/email, region-specific providers) is handled by adapters, satisfying the payment-integration driver.
weaknesses: Protection/compliance driver only partially satisfied: personal-data isolation is logical within a shared process, and no centralized audit logging is selected, which weakens ISO 27001 scoping and security-event monitoring (security QA mixed).
Bike location tracking has no allocated mechanism (S5 and bike-tracking driver partially satisfied), although the project description explicitly requires tracking bike locations.
The deployable and database form a shared failure domain; a defect in reporting can affect rider functions (availability QA mixed; availability driver partially satisfied).
Ease of use is not targeted beyond channel-specific API modules (driver partially satisfied).
qa_tensions: Data consistency and timeliness (positive) vs availability (mixed): the single transactional store that guarantees immediate, consistent state is also the shared failure domain.
Sustainability (positive) and simplicity vs security (mixed): avoiding extra runtime components also forgoes physical isolation of sensitive data and centralized audit logging.
Modifiability (slightly positive): adapters ease provider changes, but region variants require variants of the whole deployable and adding broker/tracing later requires restructuring.
arch_tradeoff: Trades fault isolation and physical data segregation for transactional simplicity and immediate consistency.
Trades use of the permitted platform technologies (broker, gateway, tracing) for a smaller operational footprint; any later move toward them is a restructuring, not an extension.
Treats the bike as a request/response adapter, trading coverage of location telemetry for not committing to an unconfirmed bike-side model.
risks: If ISO 27001 scoping or the applicable regime (EU or China) requires physical separation of personal data or centralized security logging, A1 needs structural change (evidence: A1 limitation on logical isolation; no audit-logging pattern selected).
If bikes report location continuously, the request/response bike adapter assumption fails and a location-ingestion path must be added (A1 assumption on telemetry).
Module boundary erosion without enforcement tooling could undermine both data isolation and modifiability over time (A1 limitation).
Unresolved requirement issues (rental end/return, payment timing, value of X) affect the Fleet & Rental and Payment modules (A1 limitation; shared by all alternatives).

strengths: Best overall driver coverage (9 satisfied), including full satisfaction of the protection/compliance driver through physical segregation of Identity and Payment data, pseudonymization, mTLS, audit logging and a conditional provision for the strict S1 reading (security QA positive).
Strongest fault isolation: rider-facing discovery and registration continue when Payment, Notification or Reporting degrade (availability QA positive; availability driver satisfied).
Explicit per-channel handling via BFFs (usability and portability QA positive; multi-channel and ease-of-use drivers satisfied).
Independent deployability and segregated stores support region-specific data residency and provider variation (modifiability QA positive).
weaknesses: Fewest satisfied requirements (9 of 13): neither bike location ingestion (S5) nor navigation guidance (S6) is allocated.

Consistency driver (high priority) only partially satisfied: administrator views and reports are eventually consistent and rental-payment consistency spans services via saga, resting on the unconfirmed assumption that eventual consistency is acceptable (consistency QA slightly positive).
Does not satisfy the carbon-footprint driver; it has the largest runtime footprint (sustainability QA negative).
Most components to secure, audit and keep available; gateway and broker become critical infrastructure.
qa_tensions: Security and availability (positive) vs data consistency (slightly positive): the service boundaries that isolate failures and sensitive data also introduce eventual consistency and cross-service sagas for money-bearing flows.
Security (positive) vs security operations: physical segregation narrows sensitive-data scope but multiplies the components that must themselves meet ISO 27001.
Usability/portability (positive) vs timeliness (mixed): BFFs and gateway tailor channels but add hops on every request.
arch_tradeoff: Trades transactional simplicity and immediate administrator-view consistency for fault isolation, physical data segregation and independent deployability.

Uses all permitted platform technologies, trading a higher operational and resource footprint for observability and decoupling; the main traditional motivation (independent scaling) is not evidenced, so the decomposition is justified by isolation only.
Keeps bike availability and rental creation in one service to preserve atomic registration, trading some decomposition purity for the S7 guarantee.
risks: Compensation in the rental-payment saga is not straightforward once a bike is physically unlocked (A2 limitation).
If administrators need up-to-date status (S12) the eventual-consistency assumption fails; no freshness bound is given in the requirements.
Operating an orchestration platform, broker, discovery and tracing stack in compliance with ISO 27001 is assumed but not evidenced (A2 assumption).
Unallocated bike location tracking and navigation leave a gap against an explicit project-description constraint.

strengths: Ties A1 for the most satisfied requirements (10 of 13) and is the only alternative with an explicit bike location-tracking path (Device Gateway), satisfying S5 and the bike-tracking driver, which reflects the explicit project-description constraint on tracking and QR unlocking.

Keeps A1's consistency strength: authoritative state, rental records, reporting and admin views share the core transactional store with synchronous read models (consistency driver satisfied; consistency QA positive).
Stronger security posture than A1: payment data physically isolated and centralized audit logging/tracing present (security QA slightly positive vs A1 mixed).

Boundaries placed at the evidenced variation points (payment platforms, messaging providers, bike protocols), so external failures and region-specific provider variants do not destabilize the core (modifiability and interoperability QA positive; availability QA slightly positive).
weaknesses: Navigation guidance (S6) is not allocated; hexagonal adapters are limited to payment and messaging.
Multi-channel driver only partially satisfied: one gateway entry point without channel-specific handling of device-dependent capabilities (usability and portability QA neutral).
Personal data in the core (identity, location, history) has only logical isolation, so the protection/compliance driver is partially satisfied, as in A1.
The core remains a shared failure domain for identity, rental and reporting (availability driver partially satisfied).
More runtime components than A1 (sustainability QA slightly negative; carbon-footprint driver partially satisfied).
qa_tensions: Data consistency (positive) vs availability (slightly positive): consistency-critical capabilities stay in one failure domain while only external integrations are isolated.
Security and auditability (positive/slightly positive) vs sustainability (slightly negative): physical payment isolation, broker and tracing add components.
Interoperability (positive) vs privacy: ingesting bike location telemetry during rentals adds personal location data that must be minimized under GDPR.
Modifiability (positive) vs conceptual integrity: two architectural styles coexist and need clear placement rules.
arch_tradeoff: Trades the uniformity of a single style for boundaries justified by external dependencies: consistency inside the core, isolation at the edges.

Commits to a connected-bike model (Device Gateway) to cover location tracking, trading certainty for coverage of an explicit constraint; the alternative states a fallback to a core adapter if bikes are not connected.
Uses a subset of permitted technologies (API gateway, broker, tracing) only where they serve extracted boundaries, a middle ground between A1 and A2 in footprint and isolation.
risks: The bike-side interaction is unresolved; the Device Gateway may turn out unnecessary or insufficient (A3 limitation), in which case S5 and the bike-tracking driver fall back to the same partial status as A1.
Personal data in the core may need physical separation for ISO 27001 scoping, the same risk as A1 for non-payment data.
Payment saga across the broker inherits the compensation difficulty for physically unlocked bikes, though confined to the payment step.
Gateway and broker are additional critical components that must be redundant and secured.

cross_alternative_tradeoffs: Requirements (primary criterion): A1 and A3 each satisfy 10 of 13 requirements; A2 satisfies 9. The discriminating requirements are S5 (bike location: only A3 satisfied) and S6 (navigation: only A1 satisfied). S1 and S3 are partial for all.

Consistency vs isolation: A1 and A3 keep consistency-critical state in one transactional store (consistency driver satisfied); A2 gains fault isolation and physical data segregation at the cost of eventual consistency for administrator views and cross-service sagas (consistency driver partial).
Security/compliance: A2 > A3 > A1 qualitatively (positive, slightly positive, mixed), driven by physical isolation and audit logging; A3 isolates payment data only.

Footprint/sustainability: A1 < A3 < A2 in runtime components; only A1 satisfies the carbon-footprint driver and A2 does not satisfy it. This ordering is structural, not measured, and the driver's interpretation is ambiguous.
Channel handling: A2 (BFFs) > A1 (channel-specific API modules) > A3 (single gateway entry).

Uncertainty exposure: A3's distinguishing benefit depends on the most uncertain assumption (connected bikes); A1's main gap (no location ingestion) is exposed by the same uncertainty in the opposite direction; A2's main dependency is acceptance of eventual consistency.
